summary: Thurston County, WA: 1942 smokehouse cabin, 1955 timber tower, removed about 1968; summit now holds communication towers; gate may be locked.

facts.design: Two-story 10-by-10-foot smokehouse cabin (1942), replaced in 1955 by a timber tower with a 14-by-14-foot cab
facts.status_note: Lookout removed about 1968; communication towers now stand on the summit

access.note: Johnson Creek Road gate may be locked; a 2023 trip report found it locked; WillhiteWeb says a north access is no longer allowed

visit.trail_note: Road walk of about 3.75 miles from the Johnson Creek Road gate to the summit, per the 2023 trip report

events.note: Two-story 10-by-10-foot smokehouse cabin used for fire detection
A timber tower replaced the cabin; register says 40 feet, a 1955 item says 45 feet
State began leasing the summit for a microwave facility; lookout already removed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and WillhiteWeb both give 40 feet; a July 29, 1955 item quoted on Forest Lookouts says the tower being built was 45 feet. The record uses 40 feet from the two sources that describe the finished tower, and the story flags the disagreement.

notes_for_editor: Access is recorded as restricted because of the locked gate and the no-longer-allowed north route, not a posted closure; the 2023 trip report notes a lack of signage forbidding entry. The only current-condition evidence is the January 2023 trip report and an undated WillhiteWeb caption, so the summit's present state may have changed. Brief status 'gone' and agency are correct; no corrections.
